SCAFFOLDING SCAM

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We catch a so-called businessman dealing in stolen scaffolding red-handed.

Unique Selling Point:
CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE - A CROOK DOING DODGY DEALS EXPOSED ON CAMERA!

Summary:
The South African construction industry is worth billions of rands every year. Generating jobs, building the economy and the country’s infrastructure also comes with risks.

The construction industry is not immune to criminal gangs targeting equipment and selling it on the black market. So while the industry earns big bucks, it also has big losses.

The scaffolding sector alone has lost close to R50 million in the last three years to dodgy dealers pillaging building sites.

We exposed this crime trend and catch one particular dealer Carte Blanche style with a sting and a bust.

Further information:
HOW DO YOU KNOW IF THE SCAFFOLDING IS STOLEN?
The big scaffolding players colour code their pieces, some even emboss identifying markers on the parts. It’s also very uncommon for these big players to sell off their stock – so if you find their stock being sold by another player – you know it’s stolen and can’t deny it!

THE BLACK MARKET
Stolen scaffolding can be found on Facebook Ads pages, Gumtree and OLX – these are the smaller one man band players making a quick buck off their stolen loot.

Then there are the bigger players like Scaffolding for Sale (SFS) – they appear to be a legit business, with a warehouse, a registered company and VAT number. But looks can be deceiving…. We know this all too well.

The owner, Russian born Serguei Ivanov, buys stolen scaffolding and “refurbishes” it. He’s making millions (bank accounts have been checked) because his stock costs are so low – stolen goods are cheaper.

He does sometimes buy the accessories that goes with the scaffolding pieces that are more difficult to come by – we have one of these suppliers that will go on camera.

* When the little guys have been confronted they fingered the Russian as their biggest client.

HOW DOES HE DO IT?
The Russian has a premises used solely for painting the stolen goods – getting rid of the evidence…
BUT he can’t get rid of the embossed identifying markers and if you scratch the surface – the original paint colour and rightful owner is revealed.

THE STING
We placed and order with SFS and bought a load – surprise surprise – it’s mostly stolen goods that can be identified by the rightful owners.

INSIDERS
PAINT YARD
We have an insider working at the painting yard – we have videos and photos showing how they paint the stolen stock to “refurbish” them into legitimate stock….

DRIVER
We have a driver that used to go and collect stolen goods around Pretoria and JHB – he’s just been retrenched because business is slow since the scaffolding industry has started their investigation.

WHO’s LOSING - THE INDUSTRY AND BY DEFAULT THE CONSUMER
Scaffolding is a necessary commodity in the building sector – it’s almost impossible to keep track of on a building site – this responsibility often falls to the supplier who is employed to supply, erect and breakdown the structures. If there are losses – it’s the supplier’s problem.

WHAT ARE THE COPS DOING?
NOTHING! Three stations have been involved in the investigation. There has been raids on SFS’ property and stolen stock was identified – but the cops have not returned it all to the rightful owners. In one instance stolen stock was removed and the Russian had the cheek to open a counter charge against the PI for taking “his” stock.

The Russian claims he bought it from a legitimate supplier and even supplied an invoice…. BUT – the invoice was fabricated and the company he claimed sold him the goods denies that they sold him those pieces – they even make sworn statements to that effect.

Script:


STRUCTURE SCAFFOLDING

VO Scaffolding – you drive past it every day around the city – it may not look like much but to criminal syndicates - it’s gold.

LINK: It’s easy to put up, and easy to carry away - opening the door for a lucrative black market scooping millions of rands every year… costing the industry and you the consumer in turn. [opening]

VO: The industry looses around 460 million rand to scaffolding theft in South Africa annually - adding in turn, to building costs.

Criminal gangs hit sites at night, arriving with big trucks using forklifts and even cranes to steal tons of scaffolding at a time.

Mike Els represents one of the biggest scaffolding suppliers in the country – SGB-CAPE – he believes this is not opportunistic crime – it is well orchestrated.

MIKE: We believe that the guys do get a shopping list and effectively come to sites looking for equipment which they have then got an automatic channel to market // INT1 M27

LINK: To keep track of their stock scaffolding suppliers colour code and brand their items – look here – this all belongs to one company - it’s identifiable and ownership should not be disputed [COLOURS]

VO: Despite every company having its own unique colour for their scaffolding with some parts even displaying embossed letters – these items still make it onto the black market.

Private Investigator John Luyt says second hand dealers often trade in stolen scaffolding// he has been investigating this crime trend for four years. Most scaffold companies don’t resell their equipment – it’s used until it’s scrapped.

JOHN: // They hire it out // where construction takes place, when it’s done it gets taken down and back to the yard where it gets hired out again. INT1 M20

VO: Yet you find endless ads online for second-hand scaffolding. Riaan Oosthuizen started a sideline scaffolding sales business to make some extra cash.//

He bought what he believed was second hand scaffolding to resell - but before the business could get off the ground, he was paid a visit by Luyt and the police.

RIAAN: they asked to come in to look at suspected stolen goods.// the thought never crossed my mind that it could be the scaffolding. INT1 M10

VO: But it was. And there were some tell tale signs.

LINK: // when you come across a colourful collection of scaffolding – chances are it’s stolen…. Because it wouldn’t have been sold legitimately STOLEN

VO: SGB-CAPE manufactures for their own use – they never ever sell scaffolding – new or secondhand. Their poles are painted orange and the boards are usually labelled.

DEVI: if I were to find any piece of SGB equipment anywhere – that equipment it’s in the wrong place?
MIKE: Correct – unless it’s on one of our sites – it would have been stolen. INT1 M11
DEVI: end up where?
MIKE: Being used by other small contractors or being cut up for scarp but invariable the stuff would be reblasted, repainted, rebranded and sold. INT1 M8

VO: Realising his stock was stolen goods, Riaan surrendered all of his scaffolding to the cops.

RIAAN: // I don’t want part of any criminal dealings.
DEVI: So the total value of what you lost?
RIAAN: It’s about R160 – R165 thousand… INT2 M2

VO: We went looking for Riaan’s supplier, Eddie Khuudzadombo, who operated from storage units in Midrand – but when we got there, the premises were vacant.

DEVI: What did you find here?
JOHN: Two of these storage units were full of scaffolding – mostly the orange ones that we know belongs to SGB // but different colours as well. EDDIE INT2 M2

VO: We called Eddie, to hear his side of the story.

DEVI: // you know each one is blaming the other now.
EDDIE: laughs – in fact… CALL M4// we bought it from some guys, I don’t know if it’s a group or what ….veli

VO: Eddie also handed his stock over to the police - taking a 100 thousand rand knock in the process. He cooperated with the authorities and called his supplier for another load, while Luyt and the cops waited to receive it.

JOHN: // a truck arrived with scaffolding – // he said he collects from a site in Mamelodi and in Babelegi EDDIE INT3 M1

LINK: So Eddie says that he bought his load from a guy called Veli here in Mamelodi – let’s see if we can find more answers here – just trying to follow up the trail. [VELI]

VO: Veli Mathe was also nowhere to be seen, but he did take our call.

VELI: I didn’t steal it // I don’t know what’s happening there because I didn’t go somewhere and break the fence or jump the wall…. CALL M4

VO: The police confiscated scaffolding valued at around R400 000 from Veli’s site. No proof of purchase was provided for any of the stock.

Luyt followed up on the Babelegi lead and discovered a so-called refurbishing yard operated by SFS or Scaffold for Sale, owned by Sergy Ivanov.

JOHN: We found every type of scaffolding equipment, base jacks, horizontals// the hook on boards stamped SGB. We found his spray //– they were busy spraying it – the one side in grey, the other side was still the orginal colour. INT1 M32

VO: It seems Ivanov also has some explaining to do, we went to his office in Silvertondale – where he sells new and second hand scaffolding.

DEVI: In your mind you’re not selling stolen goods – you never have sold stolen goods.
SERGY: I cant say 100% - what is stolen stuff – is it secondhand or what?
DEVI: No Stolen is stolen
SERGY: Stolen is stolen – but who say stuff is stolen? Because when I buy stuff every time ask it’s your or something else – nobody tell me stuff is stolen. INT2 M3

VO: But it’s not the first time Ivanov’s name has come up.

Adrian Nunn operates Viva Access – he had a hundred scaffolding boards valued at R65 000 stolen off a site earlier this year. Some of it was recovered at a yard in Mooikloof – also operated by Ivanov.

ADRIAN: we found all this equipment that was ours and other companies that had been sprayed grey and that equipment was finding it’s way to Silvertondale and being sold out of the warehouse there. INT1 M28

LINK: This scaffolding behind me was recovered // – it’s different colours because it actually belongs to different companies - it may look like scrap to you but this worth R350k. SMARTIE M1

DEVI: VIVA how did you end up with their scaff? INT2 M8
SERGY: it’s my scaffolding – I buy that
DEVI: yah, you bought it but it was stolen from them – that’s what they are saying.
SERGY: but he must prove // INT2 M9

VO: What Ivanov doesn’t seem to want to understand is that the different colour paints, are the identifying markers.

He claimed to have bought all material legitimately – but the invoices he provided Luyt, did not add up – the stock in the invoices don’t match the allegedly stolen stock that was recovered.

JOHN: the invoices that he supplied to us was regarding base jacks and old rusted equipment not the orange ones and the stamped one we found in his warehouse. INT1 M37

VO: SGB-CAPE property was also recovered at Ivanov’s yards. The police instructed him not to touch it until the matter was investigated and had been to court.

DEVI: // what were doing with SGB scaff –
SERGY: when I buy bulk – scaff in bulk I’m not worry about sgb INT2 M14
DEVI: Their scaff not ever up for sale – if you bought it, it means it was stolen off the sites. INT2 M20
SERGY: I am not agreeing – sorry. INT2 M15

VO: Ivanov showed us the General Conditions of Sale taken off SGB-CAPE’s website. He argued that the company does sell scaffolding.

SERGY: on that contract if you pay ownership changes when you pay full price – how that possible – how you can explain me? INT2 M19

VO: Els confirmed that they do sell material – but not scaffolding:
“We sell insulation, sheet metal products and QuikDeck. No scaffolding is sold…. SGB-Cape is a contracting division and only has scaffolding for in house use.”

An explanation Ivanov would not accept.

Interested to see if he was still trading with alleged stolen goods, we placed an order with Scaffold for Sale.

R5934 bought us a small scaffolding rig - which according to the invoice included 8 NEW hook on boards… but instead we were given refurbished boards, 7 of which were actually SGB stock.

We checked the load with Luyt.

JOHN: it’s not sandblasted as one can see you can scratch any where – and underneath you’ll find another colour.
DEVI there’s blue
JOHN: // he is still dealing in property that is clearly marked and repainted
DEVI: This is very valuable evidence then. STING M8

DEVI: // you’re not selling SGB
SERGY: no
DEVI: you sure about that?
SERGY: you know about something
DEVI: I know something
SERGY: ok that mean I sell. Ok –maybe its mistake.
DEVI: you have sold – SGB
SERGY: ok, maybe// INT2 M29
DEVI: But you shouldn’t be selling any SGB anything since this drama happened right?
SERGY: I cant answer becaseu I am little bit confused sorry – it’s true.
DEVI: …. You know how I know, because you sold it to us.
SERGY: is ok
DEVI: no is not ok – is bad – is not ok. INT2 M30 // you knew SGB was a problem and you still sold it?
SERGY: why you push me for that way? INT2 M35

VO: Ivanov argued that after police raided his premises, the alleged stolen material was set aside and he was eventually allowed to continue trading with other stock – albeit SGB stock.

He accuses Luyt of targeting his business.

JOHN: it’s not to target him – we’ve investigated all over Gauteng so far but still everything leads back to Sergi and SFS. INT1 M42

VO: But Ivanov is adamant the investigation is a witch hunt.

SERGY: I want to close my business – I see everybody push me, the gypsy radio go around , my customer torn form me because everybody say I am busy stolen stuff – but I think it is a trade war. The big company want to close us because our price is best. //INT3 M1

VO: But operators like Nunn says it’s not about competition it’s about a second hand market that makes money off theft.

ADRIAN: Lets leave stuff that has nothing to do with you alone – that’s how we used to play and that’s how we have to go forward. INT1 M38


END

 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Scaffolding may not look much – but it’s worth big bucks. And a growing black market fuels the demand for stolen items – costing the construction industry millions every year.

PROMO 2
VO: Scaffolding is worth big bucks – its reusable, hardly ever gets sold second-hand and gets scrapped when it’s unsafe to use.

MIKE: unless it’s on one of our sites – it would have been stolen. INT1 M11

VO: We investigate a black market for stolen scaffolding hitting the construction industry.


PROMO 3
VO: Construction is the lifeblood of the economy – but dodgy second hand scaffolding dealers are making big money from stolen items.

MIKE: We believe that the guys do get a shopping list and effectively come to sites looking for equipment //

VO: Carte Blanche investigates.

PROMO 4
VO: Scaffolding may not look much – but it’s worth big bucks. Criminal syndicates loot building sites selling to second-hand dealers who seem to look the other way.

SERGY: I cant say 100% - what is stolen stuff – is it secondhand or what?
DEVI: No Stolen is stolen

VO: The black market dealing in stolen scaffolding costs the construction industry millions a year. The demand drives the supply.

JOHN

VO: We follow the trial.

INT1 M32 VO: It seems Ivanov also has some explaining to do, we went to his office in Silvertondale – where he sells new and second hand scaffolding. DEVI: In your mind you’re not selling stolen goods – you never have sold stolen goods. SERGY: I cant say 100% - what is stolen stuff – is it secondhand or what? DEVI: No Stolen is stolen SERGY: Stolen is stolen – but who say stuff is stolen? Because when I buy stuff every time ask it’s your or something else – nobody tell me stuff is stolen. INT2 M3 VO: But it’s not the first time Ivanov’s name has come up. Adrian Nunn operates Viva Access – he had a hundred scaffolding boards valued at R65 000 stolen off a site earlier this year. Some of it was recovered at a yard in Mooikloof – also operated by Ivanov. ADRIAN: we found all this equipment that was ours and other companies that had been sprayed grey and that equipment was finding it’s way to Silvertondale and being sold out of the warehouse there. INT1 M28 LINK: This scaffolding behind me was recovered // – it’s different colours because it actually belongs to different companies - it may look like scrap to you but this worth R350k. SMARTIE M1 DEVI: VIVA how did you end up with their scaff? INT2 M8 SERGY: it’s my scaffolding – I buy that DEVI: yah, you bought it but it was stolen from them – that’s what they are saying. SERGY: but he must prove // INT2 M9 VO: What Ivanov doesn’t seem to want to understand is that the different colour paints, are the identifying markers. He claimed to have bought all material legitimately – but the invoices he provided Luyt, did not add up – the stock in the invoices don’t match the allegedly stolen stock that was recovered. JOHN: the invoices that he supplied to us was regarding base jacks and old rusted equipment not the orange ones and the stamped one we found in his warehouse. INT1 M37 VO: SGB-CAPE property was also recovered at Ivanov’s yards. The police instructed him not to touch it until the matter was investigated and had been to court. DEVI: // what were doing with SGB scaff – SERGY: when I buy bulk – scaff in bulk I’m not worry about sgb INT2 M14 DEVI: Their scaff not ever up for sale – if you bought it, it means it was stolen off the sites. INT2 M20 SERGY: I am not agreeing – sorry. INT2 M15 VO: Ivanov showed us the General Conditions of Sale taken off SGB-CAPE’s website. He argued that the company does sell scaffolding. SERGY: on that contract if you pay ownership changes when you pay full price – how that possible – how you can explain me? INT2 M19 VO: Els confirmed that they do sell material – but not scaffolding: “We sell insulation, sheet metal products and QuikDeck. No scaffolding is sold…. SGB-Cape is a contracting division and only has scaffolding for in house use.” An explanation Ivanov would not accept. Interested to see if he was still trading with alleged stolen goods, we placed an order with Scaffold for Sale. R5934 bought us a small scaffolding rig - which according to the invoice included 8 NEW hook on boards… but instead we were given refurbished boards, 7 of which were actually SGB stock. We checked the load with Luyt. JOHN: it’s not sandblasted as one can see you can scratch any where – and underneath you’ll find another colour. DEVI there’s blue JOHN: // he is still dealing in property that is clearly marked and repainted DEVI: This is very valuable evidence then. STING M8 DEVI: // you’re not selling SGB SERGY: no DEVI: you sure about that? SERGY: you know about something DEVI: I know something SERGY: ok that mean I sell. Ok –maybe its mistake. DEVI: you have sold – SGB SERGY: ok, maybe// INT2 M29 DEVI: But you shouldn’t be selling any SGB anything since this drama happened right? SERGY: I cant answer becaseu I am little bit confused sorry – it’s true. DEVI: …. You know how I know, because you sold it to us. SERGY: is ok DEVI: no is not ok – is bad – is not ok. INT2 M30 // you knew SGB was a problem and you still sold it? SERGY: why you push me for that way? INT2 M35 VO: Ivanov argued that after police raided his premises, the alleged stolen material was set aside and he was eventually allowed to continue trading with other stock – albeit SGB stock. He accuses Luyt of targeting his business. JOHN: it’s not to target him – we’ve investigated all over Gauteng so far but still everything leads back to Sergi and SFS. INT1 M42 VO: But Ivanov is adamant the investigation is a witch hunt. SERGY: I want to close my business – I see everybody push me, the gypsy radio go around , my customer torn form me because everybody say I am busy stolen stuff – but I think it is a trade war. The big company want to close us because our price is best. //INT3 M1 VO: But operators like Nunn says it’s not about competition it’s about a second hand market that makes money off theft. ADRIAN: Lets leave stuff that has nothing to do with you alone – that’s how we used to play and that’s how we have to go forward. INT1 M38 END PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Scaffolding may not look much – but it’s worth big bucks. And a growing black market fuels the demand for stolen items – costing the construction industry millions every year. PROMO 2 VO: Scaffolding is worth big bucks – its reusable, hardly ever gets sold second-hand and gets scrapped when it’s unsafe to use. MIKE: unless it’s on one of our sites – it would have been stolen. INT1 M11 VO: We investigate a black market for stolen scaffolding hitting the construction industry. PROMO 3 VO: Construction is the lifeblood of the economy – but dodgy second hand scaffolding dealers are making big money from stolen items. MIKE: We believe that the guys do get a shopping list and effectively come to sites looking for equipment // VO: Carte Blanche investigates. PROMO 4 VO: Scaffolding may not look much – but it’s worth big bucks. Criminal syndicates loot building sites selling to second-hand dealers who seem to look the other way. SERGY: I cant say 100% - what is stolen stuff – is it secondhand or what? DEVI: No Stolen is stolen VO: The black market dealing in stolen scaffolding costs the construction industry millions a year. The demand drives the supply. JOHN VO: We follow the trial. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We catch a so-called businessman dealing in stolen scaffolding red-handed.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE - A CROOK DOING DODGY DEALS EXPOSED ON CAMERA!
metadata.Summary: The South African construction industry is worth billions of rands every year. Generating jobs, building the economy and the country’s infrastructure also comes with risks. The construction industry is not immune to criminal gangs targeting equipment and selling it on the black market. So while the industry earns big bucks, it also has big losses. The scaffolding sector alone has lost close to R50 million in the last three years to dodgy dealers pillaging building sites. We exposed this crime trend and catch one particular dealer Carte Blanche style with a sting and a bust.
metadata.Further information: HOW DO YOU KNOW IF THE SCAFFOLDING IS STOLEN? The big scaffolding players colour code their pieces, some even emboss identifying markers on the parts. It’s also very uncommon for these big players to sell off their stock – so if you find their stock being sold by another player – you know it’s stolen and can’t deny it! THE BLACK MARKET Stolen scaffolding can be found on Facebook Ads pages, Gumtree and OLX – these are the smaller one man band players making a quick buck off their stolen loot. Then there are the bigger players like Scaffolding for Sale (SFS) – they appear to be a legit business, with a warehouse, a registered company and VAT number. But looks can be deceiving…. We know this all too well. The owner, Russian born Serguei Ivanov, buys stolen scaffolding and “refurbishes” it. He’s making millions (bank accounts have been checked) because his stock costs are so low – stolen goods are cheaper. He does sometimes buy the accessories that goes with the scaffolding pieces that are more difficult to come by – we have one of these suppliers that will go on camera. * When the little guys have been confronted they fingered the Russian as their biggest client. HOW DOES HE DO IT? The Russian has a premises used solely for painting the stolen goods – getting rid of the evidence… BUT he can’t get rid of the embossed identifying markers and if you scratch the surface – the original paint colour and rightful owner is revealed. THE STING We placed and order with SFS and bought a load – surprise surprise – it’s mostly stolen goods that can be identified by the rightful owners. INSIDERS PAINT YARD We have an insider working at the painting yard – we have videos and photos showing how they paint the stolen stock to “refurbish” them into legitimate stock…. DRIVER We have a driver that used to go and collect stolen goods around Pretoria and JHB – he’s just been retrenched because business is slow since the scaffolding industry has started their investigation. WHO’s LOSING - THE INDUSTRY AND BY DEFAULT THE CONSUMER Scaffolding is a necessary commodity in the building sector – it’s almost impossible to keep track of on a building site – this responsibility often falls to the supplier who is employed to supply, erect and breakdown the structures. If there are losses – it’s the supplier’s problem. WHAT ARE THE COPS DOING? NOTHING! Three stations have been involved in the investigation. There has been raids on SFS’ property and stolen stock was identified – but the cops have not returned it all to the rightful owners. In one instance stolen stock was removed and the Russian had the cheek to open a counter charge against the PI for taking “his” stock. The Russian claims he bought it from a legitimate supplier and even supplied an invoice…. BUT – the invoice was fabricated and the company he claimed sold him the goods denies that they sold him those pieces – they even make sworn statements to that effect. INTERVIEWS - SGB SCAFFOLDING – BIG PLAYER - SMALL LEGITIMATE COMPANY THAT SUPPLIES HIM PARTS - PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR – JOHN LUYT - INSIDER – DRIVER - INSIDER – PAINT YARD - STING - COPS - BUST WITH THE RUSSIAN

metadata.Viewing Notes: In FRYING SESSION Nicky outlined the characters through whom she plans to tell the story -- ultimately culminating in a confrontation with The Russian. The beauty/excitement of the story is in the entertaining trail of the investigation that led to the uncovering of the scam...from an end buyer that ended up with stolen goods that he didn't want to use, to the Russian who seems to be the mastermind of the scam. Nicky's narrative will follow the investigation that led SGB to uncovering the scam that is costing an ensite industry. Nicky will make the relevance to viewers clear upfront -- to explain how massive costs are passed onto consumers/builders/contractors who want use scaffolding in construction.
